thesis: Microscopic studies and applications of nuclear charge properties based on relativistic density functional theory
research_interests: Nuclear charge distributions, radii, and higher radial moments within relativistic (covariant) density functional theory.
Nuclear-structure and finite-nuclear-size effects in precision atomic physics: hydrogenlike ions, muonic atoms, bound-electron g factors, and electron scattering.
Earlier work in precision atomic calculations and quantum walks; interest in connections to quantum information and numerical quantum dynamics.
contributions: Nuclear charge radii. Studied intrinsic nucleon electromagnetic structure and quadrupole shape fluctuations to describe calcium-isotope radius evolution without local parameter readjustment [1, 2].
Muonic-atom spectra. Used microscopic charge densities to benchmark model dependence and methods for extracting charge radii, higher radial moments, and low-momentum form factors [3, 4].
Finite nuclear size and g factors. Calculated finite-nuclear-size corrections and assessed nuclear contributions to Ne isotope g-factor differences using deformation and Bayesian inference [5, S1].

Quantum information and precision atomic calculations. Master's work covered quantum walks on Sierpinski fractal networks [7], relativistic corrections for screened hydrogenlike atoms [6], and critical screening behavior [14].
skills: Programming and computing. Proficient in Fortran; working proficiency in Python (NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch), C/C++, and MATLAB. Experience with batch and multiprocessing workflows on Linux.
Nuclear-structure calculations. Use RCHB for research and modify or extend its data outputs as needed.
Dirac solvers. Maintain and use high-precision generalized pseudospectral solvers; familiar with the algorithm and kinetic-balance improvements.
Electron scattering. Independently wrote a Dirac partial-wave code for elastic electron-nucleus scattering, with reference to the open-source ELSEPA program.

Quantum dynamics and atomic structure. Simulations of quantum walks on fractal networks, including probability distributions, return probabilities, and standard deviations; precision calculations of screened one-electron systems.
Theory and statistics. Relativistic (covariant) density functional theory, Bayesian inference (MCMC), and machine-learning uncertainty quantification.
collaboration: Contributed to collaborative studies of nuclear charge-density predictions, point-proton density distributions, the DRHBc nuclear mass table, and halo-nucleus charge properties [8-13]. Assisted the advisor in supervising graduate research on halo-nucleus charge properties and finite-nuclear-size effects in confined hydrogenlike ions, with outcomes including papers [8, 9] and preprint [S2].
